intro: Everything known to be worth doing on this site, with the evidence for each. Hand-maintained on purpose — static analysis can tell you a component is unreferenced, but not whether deleting it is the right call this week. Edit this file directly: set "status": "done" to strike an item through. Numbers cited here come from tools/insight/data.json unless a file:line says otherwise.
notes: DROPPED — "Replace the devart.com root links with deep cluster links": no longer true. index.html's three https://www.devart.com/ occurrences (lines 32, 41, 58) are JSON-LD publisher/Organization url fields, where the root is correct, not anchors; the audit's cited anchors at old lines 1275-1279 do not exist in the current code. src/pages/about-insightis.jsx:233-234 already ships descriptive deep links to https://www.devart.com/dbforge/ and https://www.devart.com/data-connectivity/, and Footer.jsx:103-104 links /company/ and /vacancies/.

MOVED TO NOTES, not items — three raw entries were verified-accurate analyses recommending *against* work, so they are non-goals rather than dashboard tasks: (1) do not consolidate SpotlightChat/SpotlightSemantic/SpotlightAnomalies — all 18 definitions confirmed at the cited lines, each name splitting into three visual families of two pages, so consolidation would yield 9 components serving 2 call sites each; (2) do not consolidate Hero — 9 distinct definitions confirmed (marketing/revenue/executive/finance at :36, product/analytics at :39, ai-chat:1206, integrations:261, semantic-layer:321), each with a bespoke HeroMockup payload; (3) do not consolidate App — the page composition root, identical across the six Solutions pages only incidentally. Worth recording in AUDIT.md so a later pass does not redo the analysis.

Four raw claims were wrong and are corrected inside the merged items: href="#" occurrences are 6 not 8, and 4 of them sit inside components already slated for deletion; contact-support.jsx does render FloatingChat and AIAssistantPanel (lines 644, 646) so the dead-panel sweep covers only connectors/docs/prompt-library; Unsplash hotlinks total 24 not 25 (the 25th grep hit is prose in privacy.jsx:100); design-system/global.css sets no overflow-x, so only app.css and responsive.css contend over it.

Two cited source documents — "Insightis site UI analysis.docx" and insightis-landing-launch-pack.md — are not in this worktree; they live untracked in the main checkout at D:\Insightis Landing New. I extracted both and confirmed the specific directives quoted (the two token changes, the shared-search-component and article-FAQ notes, and launch-pack P0-1/P0-2/P2-1/P2-3). Because they are untracked, these requirements can vanish from any fresh clone — worth committing or moving into AUDIT.md.

Sequencing that the ranking alone does not express: the responsive.css load-order fix is the root cause of the h1/h2 conflict and the duplicated-global-rules item, so if the visual regression pass is funded, do it first and the other two shrink. Likewise run the two dead-code sweeps before the href="#" and Unsplash items, since deletion removes 4 of the 6 placeholder links and 8 of the 24 hotlinks for free.

Nine items are genuinely blocked and cannot start: three on legal or counsel (privacy policy wording, cookie disclosure pending the GTM-TSTTC7TZ tag list, implied-consent review), one on product sourcing the 3x accuracy claim, one on author copy for AI Chat FAQ answers 4-6, one on real blog/customer-story imagery, one on a design asset, one on an owner decision about the untracked artefacts, and the responsive.css reorder on a 31-page visual regression pass.

items.title: Reconcile the three duplicated global CSS rules across global.css, app.css and responsive.css
items.detail: Three global rules are written more than once with load order deciding the winner. The prefers-reduced-motion universal kill-switch exists in all three files and the durations disagree (0.01ms vs 0.001ms), all with !important, so two copies are unreachable. Scrollbar width is 10px in global.css and 8px in app.css, which wins. overflow-x is set in app.css (clip) and re-set in responsive.css (hidden !important, then clip !important four lines later under @supports), with the same iOS sticky-header rationale written out twice. Correction to the input: global.css sets no overflow-x, so only two files contend there.
items.evidence: prefers-reduced-motion at design-system/global.css:449, src/app.css:29 (universal selector at :35), public/assets/responsive.css:32; scrollbar at design-system/global.css:129 (`*::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 10px }`) vs src/app.css:110 (`::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 8px }`); overflow-x at src/app.css:121 (`body{overflow-x:clip}`) vs public/assets/responsive.css:162 and :167, with duplicated rationale at src/app.css:117 and responsive.css:158

items.title: Fix the contradictory :focus-visible rule — global.css sets outline:none, app.css sets a 2px outline
items.detail: Both layers define the bare :focus-visible selector with opposing values for outline (none vs 2px solid) and border-radius (--ins-radius-sm vs a hardcoded 4px). app.css wins because it comes after its own import of the design system, so global.css's outline:none is dead and the DS radius token is silently overridden by a magic number. Anyone reading global.css concludes the focus ring is box-shadow-only, which is wrong — and this is the keyboard focus indicator.
items.evidence: design-system/global.css:112 (`:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--ins-focus-ring); border-radius: var(--ins-radius-sm); }`) vs src/app.css:14-19 (`outline: 2px solid var(--ins-text-highlight, #0EC4C1); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px`)

items.title: Fix the CI catch-22 that blocks every merge request into master
items.detail: In .gitlab-ci.yml the .deploy job carries `- when: manual` with `allow_failure: false`. A manual job that has not been run counts as pending, and the merge request requires a successful pipeline — so every MR needs its staging job triggered by hand before it can merge. That is DevOps' file; raise it rather than edit it.

items.title: Load responsive.css after the bundle, or fold it in — it currently loads first
items.detail: Every shell links responsive.css in the first few lines of head while Vite injects the bundle stylesheet much later, so the override layer loads before what it overrides — which is why nearly every rule in it carries !important. That inverted cascade is the root cause of the h1/h2, overflow-x and reduced-motion conflicts listed separately. Moving the link after the bundle, or importing it from app.css, lets specificity do the work.
items.evidence: dist/index.html:15 (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/responsive.css">`, 11,970 B) vs dist/index.html:106 (bundle CSS, 199,593 B); source side index.html:8, pricing.html:7 and 29 more shells; design-system/AUDIT.md:32 documents the same load graph
items.blocked_on: Visual regression pass across all 31 pages — removing !important reliance will shift mobile layout
items.outcome: Folded onto the end of src/app.css and the <link> removed from all 31 shells, so source order gives the responsive layer the last word instead of !important compensating for load order.
